rights_note: The Met's Open Access images of public-domain works are released CC0. Used only as a reference for the kinds of trimming, cloth and hats the 1904 women's dress is drawn with (T-3553); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-14 (T-3553) from the museum's open-access image and object record: a hat of 1900 made as a wreath of small cream silk flowers with leaves, a black velvet bow at one side. A real garment, European, not of Chicago and not of anyone drawn in the town.
note: One of the T-3553 finery references (docs/RESEARCH/finery-3553/README.md): the flower hat.
what_it_supplies: silk flowers massed round a hat, and a velvet bow
what_it_does_not_supply: how any Prairie Avenue woman dressed, or the colour of any dress she owned
how often such a dress was worn on a Chicago street in 1904
